label: token right after an early q (positions 1-5)
explanation: Fires on the input step right after a q, during the original phase (or at <DEL> when q was the last original token), only when that q is early in the sequence: step t <= 5, so q is at position 0-4. The token at the firing step itself does not matter. Activation is strongest at t = 2-4 and is very large when the q is a repeat (as in x y q [q] [next]); the step after the second q is often the top activation, and the step two after a q gets weaker spillover (prev2_tok = q). It gets weaker for later positions and does not fire at t >= 6 even right after a q. It never fires in the copy phase, so q being fed back as an output does not trigger it. Outside this context there are only scattered weak activations, about 8% of activation mass and mostly in the lowest quartile.

issues: The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.941, R 0.657, F1 0.774, mass recall 0.920.
The claim that it never fires in the copy phase holds: phase==2 has 0 active steps out of 2.73M.

The early-position cutoff holds, but it is a gradual decline rather than a sharp edge. Precision of prev_tok==q by step: t=1-3 about 1.00, t=4 0.95, t=5 0.69, t=6 0.07. A q at position 4 is only partly reliable.

The <DEL> part of the explanation overclaims slightly. At the delimiter step (prev_tok==q, phase==1, t<=5) precision is 0.54 and mass recall 0.019. Restricting to phase==0 gives P 0.971 and F1 0.765, which is nearly the same.

The misses are mostly one weak background pattern. About 17k of the 39k missed steps are at t=4 with no q in the previous two steps (precision 0.045, 2.9% of mass, almost all in the lowest quartile). Spillover two steps after a q (prev2_tok==q) has precision 0.18 and 4% of mass. Neither can be added without hurting F1, so this counts as low-mass noise.
The label 'positions 1-5' refers to the firing step t (1-5), while the explanation says the q is at positions 0-4. The two are consistent but could be read the wrong way.
